| [CLAIM-814](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-814.md) | Reservoir gain does not trade memory for noise | A correction to A15 §2 of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws", and the gap it leaves. A illustrates a memory–noise tradeoff with x(t+1) = a x(t) + u(t) + η(t): as a → 1 memory half-life and noise variance both diverge, so "criticality amplifies both information and uncertainty". Input and noise enter through the same filter, so the state's signal-to-noise ratio is s²/σ² at every a, and the total linear memory capacity, summed over lags, is s²/(s²+σ²) at every a: the gain redistributes a fixed capacity across lags and trades nothing against noise. An interior optimum appears only for a task that weights lags: for recall k steps back it is a = √(k/(k+1)). With readout noise, capacity rises toward a = 1. Checked analytically and by simulation. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
